title: “Impact of Zika and Chikungunya Viruses on Spontaneous Abortions: Insights from a Reference Maternity Hospital”
content: To investigate the association between spontaneous abortion and ZIKV and CHIKV infection. Methods: The study population consisted of pregnant women who had a miscarriage in 2015, 2016 and 2017, comprising a quantitative of 30 women who were treated at the referral hospital. The study material paraffin-embedded samples containing material from the, corresponding to placental and fetal remains tested by hematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemistry techniques for ZIKV and CHIKV. Results: Regarding the sociodemographic, clinical and obstetric characteristics of the patients, they correspond to: the age group between 20 and 29 years of age; brown color; women who had abortions for the first time; miscarriages occurred in the first trimester of pregnancy; women belonging to the metropolitan region of Belém; diagnosed with incomplete abortion and who underwent uterine curettage procedure. Regarding the histopathologic and immunohistochemical findings, an inflammatory infiltrate rich in neutrophils and lymphocytes, among others, was found in endometrial fragments and chorionic membranes. In addition, placental areas consisting of edema, necrosis and hemorrhage were found. Conclusion: The study identified ZIKV and CHIKV in 40 % (n = 12) of samples from spontaneous abortion specimes, and CHIKV was the most prevalent virus in the study, representing 36.11 % of the total specimes, with reddish granular material in the cytoplasm of decidua cells and placental villi, that the viruses may be present in these regions of the placenta.
